mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is declining but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by >0.3pp but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth combined with rising employment suggests inefficient economic growth, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows and PAYEMS increases but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates during a monetary tightening cycle may lead to decreased corporate profitability and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth suggests a robust supply chain, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is strong but SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates reduced consumer demand, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST falls below 800 but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPI) without corresponding increases in wages (UNRATE) may lead to decreased consumer purchasing power and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises and UNRATE does not increase but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales (RSAFS) during a late-cycle expansion may indicate overextension in consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS exceeds 350000 but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
